title: Abba Yudan Rama'ah
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Vayikra Rabbah 5:4 relates why he was called Rammai (“deceiver”): he gave generously in order to outwit the people into giving generously too, and he would contribute an amount equal to the total collected from all the people of the city. Resh Lakish showed him great honor and seated him beside him. In Bamidbar Rabbah (printed locator: פ״דח), he is called Avin Rama’ah. The passage derives from the Jerusalem Talmud, Horayot chapter 3, halakhah 4, and reads as follows: “Resh Lakish went to Botzra, and there was there one of their leading men, a ‘deceiver’. Far be it that he was a deceiver; rather, he used cleverness in the performance of good deeds. Resh Lakish took him and seated him beside him.” A textual error occurred in Yuchasin; it should read: Avin of Tzippori before ר״י ben Elazar; Avin Rama’ah, in Horayot chapter 3, lived in the time of Resh Lakish. This removes the difficulty raised by Seder HaDorot.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: The parallel in [Vayikra Rabbah 5:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Vayikra_Rabbah.5.4), Midrash Rabbah—TE, names Abba Yudan Rammai and R. Shimon ben Lakish (Resh Lakish). [Yerushalmi Horayot 3:4:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Horayot.3.4.5), Guggenheimer’s Hebrew edition (De Gruyter, 1999–2015), likewise names R. Shimon ben Lakish and describes matching the community’s total pledge. These passages support expanding Hyman’s רש״בל and ר״ל as Resh Lakish. ר״י בן אלעזר remains unexpanded because its initial alone does not identify the name securely.

The English ‘Far be it that he was a deceiver’ follows חס ליה in the cited Horayot edition and וחס ושלום in the Vayikra parallel. The supplied Hyman transcription instead has חם ליה, which led the earlier draft to ‘he saw’. This is an explicit source-supported correction in translation; the Hebrew transcription has not been changed. Hyman’s חד רבהון רמיא is rendered ‘one of their leading men, a “deceiver”’, without assigning a name to רבהון.

Hyman’s Bamidbar Rabbah label is פ״דח. The corresponding 4:8 in Midrash Rabbah—TE concerns the firstborn and Levites, not this anecdote; the inspected chapter 4 did not establish the Avin Rama’ah parallel. His label and claim are therefore preserved, with no replacement number proposed. The expansions ט״ס as ‘textual error’ and סה״ד as Seder HaDorot are conventional contextual readings. Hyman’s identification and proposed Yuchasin correction remain attributed to him.
